q: What is the earliest age at which you can apply for a Pennsylvania learner's permit?
exp: Pennsylvania does not accept a permit application before the applicant's 16th birthday.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Applying for a Learner's Permit, pp. 1 to 2

q: How many questions are on the Pennsylvania knowledge test?
exp: The knowledge test is 18 multiple choice questions on signs, laws and safe driving.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Tests, pp. 5 to 6

q: How many correct answers do you need to pass the Pennsylvania knowledge test?
exp: You must answer 15 of the 18 questions correctly, so you can miss no more than 3.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Tests, pp. 5 to 6

q: Who may supervise a 16-year-old driving on a Pennsylvania learner's permit?
a: Any licensed driver who is at least 18
b: Any passenger who is at least 21, licensed or not
c: A licensed driver who is at least 25
d: A licensed driver who is at least 21, or a licensed parent, guardian or spouse who is at least 18
exp: The supervisor must be licensed and at least 21, or be a licensed parent, guardian, person acting as a parent, or spouse aged 18 or more.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Junior Learner's Permit and Junior Driver's License, pp. 3 to 4

q: Before the road test, how many hours of supervised driving must a driver under 18 complete in Pennsylvania?
a: 65 hours, including at least 10 at night and 5 in bad weather
exp: Drivers under 18 need 65 hours of practice, with no fewer than 10 night hours and 5 bad weather hours.
src: 75 Pa.C.S. 1505(e); PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, p. 1

q: How long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before taking the road test?
exp: A minor must wait six months from the permit issue date before the road test.
src: 75 Pa.C.S. 1505(e); PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, p. 1

q: During which hours may a junior license holder NOT drive without a parent, guardian or adult spouse, unless an exception applies?
exp: Junior drivers may not drive from 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. without a parent, guardian or adult spouse, except for work, volunteer fire company or public service.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Junior Learner's Permit and Junior Driver's License, pp. 3 to 4

q: For the first six months on a junior license, how many passengers under 18 who are not immediate family may you carry without a parent or guardian in the car?
exp: The limit is one such passenger for the first six months, rising to three after that if your record is clean.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Junior Learner's Permit and Junior Driver's License, pp. 3 to 4

q: A junior driver collects 6 points on their driving record. What happens?
exp: Drivers under 18 lose their license for 90 days at 6 or more points, or for going 26 mph or more over the limit.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Junior Learner's Permit and Junior Driver's License, pp. 3 to 4; PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 4, Pennsylvania's Point System

q: In the parallel parking part of the Pennsylvania road test, how many adjustments are you allowed?
d: As many as you need in two minutes
exp: You get one attempt to park in the 24 by 8 foot space, using no more than three adjustments.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Tests, pp. 5 to 6

q: Which form is the Pennsylvania learner's permit application?
exp: The Non-Commercial Learner's Permit Application is form DL-180; a health care provider completes the medical section.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Applying for a Learner's Permit, pp. 1 to 2

q: An applicant under 18 must bring which form signed by a parent, guardian or adult spouse?
b: DL-59, the change to a regular license
d: DL-180TD, the Parent or Guardian Consent Form
exp: The DL-180TD gives adult consent; if the signer cannot come along, it must be notarized.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Applying for a Learner's Permit, pp. 1 to 2

q: The physical exam on the permit application may be done no earlier than:
exp: The health care provider may complete the DL-180 no earlier than six months before the applicant turns 16.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Applying for a Learner's Permit, pp. 1 to 2

q: Your parent cannot come with you to the Driver License Center. What must happen to the consent form?
a: Your parent must call the center
b: The parent must sign it in front of a notary
c: Any adult relative may sign it at the center
exp: If the consenting adult cannot be there, the DL-180TD must be signed in the presence of a notary.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Applying for a Learner's Permit, pp. 1 to 2

q: Which documents does PennDOT accept as proof of your birth date and identity?
exp: Proof of date of birth and identity must be originals; photocopies are not accepted.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Applying for a Learner's Permit, pp. 1 to 2

q: Applicants 18 or older must bring how many proofs of Pennsylvania residency for a permit?
exp: Adult applicants show two proofs of residency, such as utility bills, a lease or a W-2.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Applying for a Learner's Permit, pp. 1 to 2

q: You fail the knowledge test on a Monday. When is the earliest you may retake it?
b: The same day at another center
exp: A failed knowledge test may be retaken the following business day, and only one attempt is allowed per day at any location.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Tests, pp. 5 to 6

q: Once issued, a Pennsylvania learner's permit is valid for:
exp: The learner's permit is valid for one year from the issue date.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Applying for a Learner's Permit, pp. 1 to 2; 75 Pa.C.S. 1505(d)

q: A driver under 18 on a learner's permit may carry how many passengers?
a: Only one passenger besides the supervisor
c: No more than the number of seat belts in the car
d: Any number if the supervisor agrees
exp: Under-18 drivers may never carry more passengers than there are seat belts.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Junior Learner's Permit and Junior Driver's License, pp. 3 to 4

q: Where must the supervising driver sit when you drive on a learner's permit?
c: In the back seat on the right
exp: The supervising driver must ride in the front seat beside the learner.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Junior Learner's Permit and Junior Driver's License, pp. 3 to 4

q: Which form does a parent or guardian sign to certify that a teen has finished the 65 hours of practice?
exp: The DL-180C certifies the 65 hours of behind-the-wheel practice and must be brought to the road test.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Tests, pp. 5 to 6

q: After six months on a junior license with a clean record, how many non-family passengers under 18 may you carry without a parent present?
exp: The limit rises to three after six months, unless you caused a crash or were convicted of a driving violation.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Junior Learner's Permit and Junior Driver's License, pp. 3 to 4

q: Which junior driver keeps the one-passenger limit for good, even after six months?
a: One who drives a car with five seat belts
b: One who has a part-time job
c: One who was partly at fault in a crash
d: One who passed the road test on the second try
exp: The higher passenger limit never applies to a junior driver who was partly or fully at fault in a crash or convicted of any driving violation.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Junior Learner's Permit and Junior Driver's License, pp. 3 to 4

q: A junior driver works until midnight. How may they legally drive home alone?
b: By driving with hazard lights on
c: Only with a friend who is 21 in the car
d: By carrying a notarized affidavit or employer certificate showing the work schedule
exp: Work, public service and volunteer fire company duties are exceptions if the driver carries the required affidavit or certificate.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Junior Learner's Permit and Junior Driver's License, pp. 3 to 4

q: A junior driver is convicted of going 26 mph over the speed limit. What is the result?
exp: A junior driver convicted of 26 mph or more over the limit is suspended for 90 days.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Junior Learner's Permit and Junior Driver's License, pp. 3 to 4

q: Which is NOT required to move from a junior license to a regular license before age 18?
a: Holding the junior license for one year
b: Taking the road test a second time
c: Passing an approved driver training course
d: No at-fault crashes and no convictions for one year
exp: The early upgrade needs a year on the junior license, approved driver training, a clean year and parental consent, not a second road test.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Junior Learner's Permit and Junior Driver's License, pp. 3 to 4

q: If you never apply to upgrade, when does a Pennsylvania junior license become a regular license?
d: Only after a second road test
exp: A junior license turns into a regular license automatically at age 18.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Junior Learner's Permit and Junior Driver's License, pp. 3 to 4

q: Which license class covers an ordinary passenger car in Pennsylvania?
exp: Class C covers passenger cars, pickups and vans and has a minimum age of 16.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Classes of Driver's Licenses, p. 4

q: How do you schedule a non-commercial road test in Pennsylvania?
a: Online on the PennDOT Driver and Vehicle Services site or by phone
exp: Road tests require an appointment, made online or by calling 1-800-423-5542.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Tests, pp. 5 to 6

q: What happens if the car you bring to the road test has an expired inspection sticker?
b: You will not be allowed to take the test
c: You pay a fine and test anyway
d: You test but cannot get the license that day
exp: The examiner checks registration, insurance and inspection first; an unsafe or out-of-inspection car means no test.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Tests, pp. 5 to 6

q: Which is an automatic fail on the Pennsylvania road test?
a: Driving 5 mph under the limit in a school zone
d: Asking the examiner to repeat an instruction
exp: Failing to signal, breaking a traffic law, causing a crash and dangerous driving are listed reasons for failing.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Tests, pp. 5 to 6

q: You cannot make the parking brake or the defroster work when the examiner asks. What is the result?
a: You lose a few points but continue
c: The examiner shows you and you continue
exp: Failing to operate any vehicle control properly results in a failed road test.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Tests, pp. 5 to 6

q: A driver under 18 fails the road test. How long must they wait to retest?
exp: PennDOT requires a seven-day wait before a driver under 18 retakes the road test.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Tests, pp. 5 to 6

q: How many road test attempts do you get on one learner's permit?
exp: You have three chances per permit; after the third failure you must apply to extend it with form DL-31.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Tests, pp. 5 to 6

q: Which of these is optional for a Pennsylvania driver?
b: A vision screening for a first license
d: An original birth or identity document
exp: REAL ID is optional in Pennsylvania; a standard license is still valid for driving.
src: pa.gov/services/dmv/apply-for-real-id

q: What is the PennDOT fee for a learner's permit together with the first four-year license?
exp: The $45.50 fee covers the permit and the first four-year license.
src: pa.gov/agencies/dmv/resources/payments-and-fees

q: A 25-year-old first-time driver gets a learner's permit. Which rule does NOT apply to them?
a: The six-month waiting period before the road test
b: Driving only with a qualified supervisor
exp: The six-month holding period and the 65-hour certificate apply only to drivers under 18.
src: 75 Pa.C.S. 1505(e); PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, p. 1

q: A visitor holds a valid license from Brazil. How long may they drive in Pennsylvania on it?
b: Up to one year from entering the U.S., or until it expires if sooner
d: As long as the license is valid
exp: Foreign license holders may drive for up to one year from entry, or until their license expires, whichever comes first.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Who Needs a Pennsylvania Driver's License, p. 3

q: A license from which of these countries can be transferred in Pennsylvania without the knowledge and road tests?
exp: Pennsylvania has reciprocity with France, Germany, South Korea and Taiwan; a vision test is still required.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Who Needs a Pennsylvania Driver's License, p. 3

q: If your vision does not meet the standard at the Driver License Center, what are you given?
a: A permit restricted to daylight with no further steps
b: An automatic denial for one year
c: A retest the next business day
d: Form DL-102, to have an eye doctor examine you
exp: The examiner gives you the Report of Eye Examination (DL-102) for an eye doctor or physician to complete.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Pennsylvania Vision Standards, p. 3

q: A new resident's out-of-state license expired eight months ago. What must they do?
a: Apply for a learner's permit and pass the knowledge and road tests
b: Transfer it with a vision test only
c: Pay a late fee and transfer it
exp: Licenses expired more than six months cannot be transferred; the driver starts with a learner's permit.
src: pa.gov/services/dmv/transfer-a-drivers-license-from-another-state

q: What is the speed limit in a Pennsylvania school zone when the yellow lights on the sign are flashing?
exp: Pennsylvania school zones are 15 mph when the lights flash or during the posted times.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 2, School Zone Signals, p. 9

q: How many points does speeding in a Pennsylvania school zone add to your record?
exp: Exceeding the school zone limit brings 3 points plus a fine.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 2, School Zone Signals, p. 9

q: When must you have your headlights on in a Pennsylvania work zone?
d: In every posted work zone, at any time of day
exp: Pennsylvania law requires headlights in all posted work zones, not only active ones.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 2, Work Zone Signs, p. 18

q: In a Pennsylvania active work zone, what happens to fines for speeding?
d: They are replaced by a warning
exp: Fines double for speeding and certain other violations in an active, posted work zone.

q: How fast over the limit must you go in a Pennsylvania active work zone to face a 15-day license suspension?
exp: A conviction for exceeding the limit by 11 mph or more in an active work zone brings a 15-day suspension.

q: Which sign marks the start of an active work zone in Pennsylvania?
exp: These signs are placed at the start and end of an active work zone, where workers are present.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 2, Work Zone Signs, p. 18

q: An automated work zone speed camera in Pennsylvania records you 12 mph over the limit for the first time. What happens?
d: The owner receives a written warning
exp: The first camera violation brings a written warning; the second is $75 and the third and later are $150, with no points.

q: Do daytime running lights satisfy Pennsylvania's work zone headlight rule?
a: No, the headlights must be turned on
c: Yes, if the car is light colored
exp: The law requires headlights, not just daytime running lights, when driving through work zones.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3, Work Zones, p. 54

q: In Pennsylvania, when may you turn right on a steady red light?
a: Without stopping if no one is coming
b: After a full stop, yielding to pedestrians and traffic, unless a sign prohibits it
c: Only when a green arrow is also lit
exp: Right on red is allowed after stopping and yielding, unless NO TURN ON RED is posted.

q: In Pennsylvania, when is a left turn on a steady red light allowed?
a: From any street when no traffic is coming
b: From a two-way street onto a one-way street
c: After a full stop, but only when both streets are one-way
exp: A left on red is legal only from one one-way street onto another, after a full stop and with no sign forbidding it.

q: You face a steady red arrow pointing right in Pennsylvania. What may you do?
b: Never turn until the arrow turns green
c: Back up and use another lane
d: Stop, then turn right if it is clear and no sign forbids it
exp: The manual says the same turns on red allowed for a steady red signal are allowed for a steady red arrow, after a stop.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 2, Red, Yellow and Green Traffic Lights and Arrows, p. 7

q: Before a legal right turn on red in Pennsylvania, what must you do first?
d: Wait for the pedestrian signal to turn red
exp: Every turn on red starts with a full stop, then yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic.

q: You are in the left lane of a one-way street at a red light, and the cross street is also one-way to the left. No sign is posted. What may you do?
c: Wait for green; left on red is never legal
exp: Pennsylvania allows a left on red from a one-way street onto a one-way street after stopping and yielding.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3, Turning Right at a Red Light, p. 45

q: You approach a police car stopped on the shoulder with its lights flashing on a four-lane Pennsylvania highway. What does the law require?
c: Move to a lane not next to it, or slow to at least 20 mph below the limit if you cannot
exp: The Move Over law requires a nonadjacent lane, or 20 mph or more under the posted limit when you cannot move over.

q: Pennsylvania's Move Over law also protects a disabled vehicle marked with at least how many warnings, such as hazard lights or flares?
exp: A disabled vehicle is covered when marked with at least two signal lamps, flares, caution signs or similar devices.

q: What is the maximum fine for a first violation of Pennsylvania's Move Over law?
exp: The statute sets fines up to $500 for a first offense, $1,000 for a second and $2,000 for a third or later.

q: How many points does a Move Over law conviction add to a Pennsylvania driving record?
exp: A person convicted under the Move Over law has 2 points assessed.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3, Move Over Law, p. 59

q: A Pennsylvania school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm out. How far from the bus must you stop?
exp: Drivers must stop at least 10 feet away, whether behind the bus or approaching it.

q: When may you NOT have to stop for a Pennsylvania school bus with red lights flashing?
a: When you are on a two-lane road coming toward the bus
c: When you are late for school
d: When you are on the opposite roadway of a divided highway with a physical median
exp: The only exception is the other side of a divided highway separated by a barrier, guide rail or median.

q: What is the license penalty for failing to stop for a Pennsylvania school bus with red lights flashing?
exp: Failing to stop brings a 60-day suspension, 5 points and a fine.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 4, Pennsylvania's Point System; 75 Pa.C.S. 1535(a)

q: A Pennsylvania school bus ahead begins flashing its yellow (amber) lights. What should you do?
a: Speed up to pass before it stops
b: Slow down and prepare to stop
d: Change lanes and keep your speed
exp: Flashing amber lights mean the bus is preparing to stop; pass only with caution and be ready to stop.

q: You stopped for a school bus. When may you move again?
a: As soon as the children are on the bus
c: When the red lights stop flashing, the stop arm is withdrawn and the children are safe
d: When the driver waves you on, even with lights flashing
exp: Stay stopped until the red lights go off, the arm is pulled in and the children have reached a safe place.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3, School Buses, p. 58

q: You are at an intersection and a school bus is stopped on the cross street with red lights flashing. What must you do?
a: Proceed if you are turning away from the bus
exp: Drivers approaching an intersection where a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing must stop.

q: In Pennsylvania, before making a U-turn, how far away must approaching drivers be?
exp: Choose a spot where drivers from every direction are at least 500 feet away and can see you.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3, U-Turns, p. 45

q: Where is a U-turn illegal in Pennsylvania?
b: On a curve or near the crest of a hill
c: At every intersection with a signal
exp: U-turns are not allowed on curves, near the top of a hill, or where a NO U-TURN sign is posted.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3, U-Turns, p. 45

q: You miss your exit on a Pennsylvania Interstate. What should you do?
a: Make a U-turn through the median
d: Stop and wait for a gap to reverse
exp: Never turn around through the median or back up; go to the next exit.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3 Review Questions, p. 73

q: When is a U-turn legal in Pennsylvania where no sign prohibits it?
c: Only with a police officer's permission
d: Only when it can be made without endangering other traffic
exp: U-turns are allowed only if they can be made safely, with traffic at least 500 feet away and able to see you.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3, U-Turns, p. 45

q: What is the highest speed limit posted anywhere in Pennsylvania?
exp: The maximum speed limit in Pennsylvania is 70 mph, on freeways posted for it.
src: 75 Pa.C.S. 3362(a)(1.1); PUB 95, Ch. 3, Posted Speed Limits, p. 39

q: Unless signs show otherwise, what is the speed limit in a Pennsylvania urban district?
exp: The statute sets 35 mph in any urban district unless another limit is posted.

q: Where no other limit applies or is posted, what is Pennsylvania's general maximum speed?
exp: 55 mph applies in all locations not covered by another limit.

q: What is the speed limit on a local road in a Pennsylvania residence district, unless posted otherwise?
exp: On local highways in residence districts that are not numbered routes, the limit is 25 mph.

q: You drive at the posted limit in heavy fog. Can you still be ticketed in Pennsylvania?
a: Yes, for driving too fast for conditions
b: No, the posted limit is always legal
exp: Posted limits are for ideal conditions; you can be cited for driving too fast for conditions.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3, Managing Speed, p. 38

q: How many points does speeding 11 to 15 mph over the limit add to a Pennsylvania record?
exp: The point schedule assigns 2 points for 6 to 10 mph over, 3 for 11 to 15 and 4 for 16 to 25.

q: What following distance does the Pennsylvania Driver's Manual teach for dry pavement?
exp: The manual's space cushion ahead is a 4-second following distance on dry pavement.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3, Keep a Space Cushion Ahead, p. 35

q: On wet roads, the Pennsylvania manual says to slow down and increase your following distance to:
exp: Reduce speed by 5 to 10 mph on wet roads and allow 5 or 6 seconds of following distance.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3, Driving in Bad Weather, p. 41

q: How much should you slow down on wet roads, according to the Pennsylvania manual?
exp: The manual advises cutting speed by 5 to 10 mph on wet roads.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3, Driving in Bad Weather, p. 41

q: You pass a pole less than 4 seconds after the car ahead of you passed it, on dry pavement. What does that mean?
exp: If you reach the marker in under four seconds, you are following too closely.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3, Keep a Space Cushion Ahead, p. 35

q: How should your following distance change in a work zone, per the Pennsylvania manual?
d: It does not matter at low speed
exp: Rear-end crashes are the most common in work zones, so the manual says to double your following distance.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3, Work Zones, p. 54

q: Which Pennsylvania highway has the state's best known reversible HOV lanes?
exp: The I-279 Parkway North HOV lanes run between Downtown Pittsburgh and the North Hills.
src: PennDOT District 11 news releases, 2023 and 2025, pa.gov

q: The I-279 HOV lanes are reversible. Which way do they carry traffic in the weekday morning rush?
exp: The reversible lanes run inbound in the morning peak and outbound in the evening peak.
src: PennDOT District 11, I-279 HOV lanes; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_279

q: You reach the entrance to a reversible lane and see a closed gate. What should you do?
b: Stay out and use the regular lanes
c: Wait for the gate to open while stopped in traffic
d: Enter if there is no oncoming traffic
exp: A closed gate or red X means the lane is not open in your direction.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 2, Lane Use Control Signals, p. 8

q: In Pennsylvania, how close to a fire hydrant may you park?
exp: Parking is banned within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3, Parking, p. 53

q: In Pennsylvania, you may not park within how many feet of a crosswalk at an intersection?
exp: No stopping or parking within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3, Parking, p. 53

q: In Pennsylvania, you may not park within how many feet of a stop sign at the side of the road?
exp: Parking is banned within 30 feet of a flashing signal, stop sign, yield sign or traffic control device at the roadside.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3, Parking, p. 53

q: In Pennsylvania, how far from the nearest rail of a railroad crossing must you park?
exp: No parking within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3, Parking, p. 53

q: When parallel parking at a curb in Pennsylvania, how close must your wheels be?
c: No more than 12 inches from the curb
exp: Park as close to the curb as possible, no more than 12 inches away.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3, Parallel Parking Tips, p. 53

q: In Pennsylvania, you may not park within how many feet of a fire station driveway?
exp: Parking is not allowed within 20 feet of a driveway entrance to a fire station.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3, Parking, p. 53

q: Which of these is a legal place to park in Pennsylvania, if no sign says otherwise?
a: At a curb 40 feet from a stop sign
d: Next to a car already parked at the curb
exp: Bridges, crosswalks and double parking are banned; 40 feet is beyond the 30-foot stop sign limit.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3, Parking, p. 53

q: What is the fine for parking in a Pennsylvania disability space without a plate or placard?
exp: Unlawful parking in a disability space is a summary offense with a $50 to $200 fine, and the car may be towed.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 5, Laws and Related Issues

q: In Pennsylvania, how much space must you leave when passing a bicycle?
exp: Pennsylvania requires at least 4 feet between your car and a bicycle when passing.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 5, Laws and Related Issues, Safe Passing

q: To give a cyclist 4 feet in Pennsylvania, may you cross a double yellow line?
c: Only if the cyclist signals you
d: Yes, if the other lane is clear and it is safe
exp: The law lets you cross the double yellow line to pass a bicycle when it is safe.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 5, Laws and Related Issues, Safe Passing

q: A cyclist is ahead on your right and an oncoming car is near. What does the Pennsylvania manual advise?
a: Slow behind the cyclist, let the oncoming car pass, then pass with at least 4 feet
c: Sound your horn so the cyclist moves over
d: Pass with 2 feet since a car is coming
exp: Handle one hazard at a time: let the oncoming vehicle go, then move left and leave at least 4 feet.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3, Sharing the Road, p. 45

q: After a Pennsylvania crash in which no one is hurt and both cars can be driven, which must you do?
a: Leave if the damage looks small
c: Stop and exchange names, addresses, registration and insurance information
exp: Every driver in a crash must stop and exchange information; police are needed for injuries, deaths or towing.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 4, Pennsylvania's Point System, Crashes

q: When must you call police after a Pennsylvania crash?
b: After every crash, even a scratch
d: When anyone is injured or killed, or a vehicle must be towed
exp: Call police if anyone is hurt or killed or a vehicle needs to be towed.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 4, Pennsylvania's Point System, Crashes

q: If police do not investigate a crash with an injury or a towed vehicle, you must send PennDOT form AA-600 within:
exp: The Driver's Accident Report (AA-600) must be sent to PennDOT within 5 days.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 4, Pennsylvania's Point System, Crashes

q: You back into an unattended parked car in Pennsylvania and cannot find the owner. What must you do?
a: Drive away if no one saw
b: Leave a note with your name, phone number, date and time, and call police
d: Report it to your insurer only
exp: Leave a note with the date, time, your name and a phone number, and notify police.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 4, Pennsylvania's Point System, Crashes

q: In Pennsylvania, when must your headlights be on during the day?
c: Whenever your wipers are on because of weather
exp: Headlights are required whenever wipers are in continuous or intermittent use because of weather.
src: PUB 95, Ch. 3, Headlight/Windshield Wiper Law, p. 43

q: At what BAC is a driver 21 or older considered under the influence in Pennsylvania?
exp: For drivers of legal drinking age, DUI starts at a BAC of 0.08 percent.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 4, DUI penalty tables

q: At what BAC is a driver under 21 considered under the influence in Pennsylvania?
exp: Pennsylvania's zero tolerance rule makes 0.02 percent DUI for drivers under 21.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 4, DUI penalty tables; PUB 95, Ch. 3, Alcohol and Driving, p. 33

q: What is the BAC limit for a commercial driver in Pennsylvania?
exp: Commercial drivers are DUI at 0.04 percent and are penalized at the high rate.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 4, DUI penalty tables

q: What happens in Pennsylvania if you refuse a chemical test when arrested for DUI, with no prior offenses?
a: Nothing, if you are later found not guilty
c: Your license is suspended for one year
exp: Refusal brings a one-year suspension even if you are found not guilty of DUI.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 4, Pennsylvania's Point System, Implied Consent

q: A Pennsylvania driver with a prior DUI refuses a breath test. How long is the refusal suspension?
exp: With a prior DUI or refusal, the refusal suspension is 18 months.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 4, Pennsylvania's Point System, Implied Consent

q: In Pennsylvania, a chemical test refusal is penalized at which DUI tier?
d: No tier; it is only a fine
exp: Refusals are treated under the highest rate penalties.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 4, DUI penalty tables

q: A first-offense Pennsylvania DUI at a BAC of 0.12 percent falls in which tier?
exp: The high rate tier covers BAC 0.10 to 0.159 percent.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 4, DUI penalty tables

q: What is the license penalty for a first-offense high rate DUI (0.10 to 0.159) in Pennsylvania?
exp: A first high rate offense brings a 12-month suspension plus 2 days to 6 months in jail.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 4, DUI penalty tables

q: What is the minimum jail time for a first-offense highest rate DUI (0.16 or more) in Pennsylvania?
exp: The highest rate first offense carries 3 days to 6 months in jail and a $1,000 to $5,000 fine.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 4, DUI penalty tables

q: Which program is required for a first or second Pennsylvania DUI at any BAC level?
exp: Alcohol Highway Safety School is required for first or second offenses at every level.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 4, DUI penalty tables

q: A 19-year-old in Pennsylvania is convicted of a first DUI at 0.03 percent BAC. What license penalty applies?
exp: Under 21 at 0.02 or more is punished at the high rate tier: 2 days to 6 months jail, $500 to $5,000 and one year suspension.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 4, DUI penalty tables

q: In Pennsylvania, may a passenger drink an open beer in a private car on a public road?
a: Yes, only the driver is restricted
b: Yes, if the driver is sober
c: No, drivers and passengers both may not
exp: Pennsylvania's open container law covers both the operator and occupants of a vehicle on a highway.

q: Pennsylvania's open container law has an exception for passengers in which vehicle?
c: A private car parked at a red light
d: A limousine or taxi used for paid passenger transport
exp: Passengers in vehicles used mainly to carry paying passengers, such as buses, taxis and limousines, are exempt.

q: Under Pennsylvania's Paul Miller's Law, may you hold your phone while stopped at a red light?
a: No, the ban applies even when stopped in traffic or at a light
b: Yes, the car is not moving
c: Yes, if the call lasts under a minute
exp: Driving includes being temporarily stopped for traffic or a signal, so handheld use is banned then too.
src: 75 Pa.C.S. 3316.1; PSP news release, June 12, 2026

q: What is the fine for violating Pennsylvania's handheld device law?
exp: A violation is a summary offense with a $50 fine plus costs.
src: 75 Pa.C.S. 3316.1(c); PSP news release, June 12, 2026

q: Which phone use is allowed for a Pennsylvania driver while driving?
b: Reading a text at a red light
d: Scrolling a map in your hand
exp: Hands-free technology for calls, navigation and music is allowed; holding the device is not.
src: PSP news release, June 12, 2026; 75 Pa.C.S. 3316.1

q: In an emergency, may a Pennsylvania driver use a handheld phone?
b: Only after stopping on an Interstate shoulder for 10 minutes
d: Yes, to contact police or emergency services
exp: Both phone laws allow contacting law enforcement or emergency services to prevent injury or damage.

q: What is the fine for texting while driving in Pennsylvania?
exp: The anti-texting law is a primary summary offense with a $50 fine.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 5, Laws and Related Issues, Texting; 75 Pa.C.S. 3316

q: Under Pennsylvania's DUI law, can a driver below 0.08 percent still be convicted of DUI?
b: Yes, if their driving shows they are impaired
exp: Lower BAC levels can still lead to a DUI conviction when driving is erratic.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 4, DUI penalty tables

q: In Pennsylvania, who must wear a seat belt in the back seat?
a: No one in the back seat
exp: The driver and front seat passengers must buckle, and passengers 8 to 17 must buckle in every seat.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 5, Laws and Related Issues, Seat Belt Law; 75 Pa.C.S. 4581

q: Who is responsible for making sure a 15-year-old passenger is buckled in Pennsylvania?
b: The passenger's parent, even if not in the car
exp: Drivers are responsible for securing children and passengers under 18.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 5, Laws and Related Issues, Child Restraint Law

q: Until what age must a Pennsylvania child ride in a rear-facing car seat?
a: Under 2, until the child outgrows the seat's limits
exp: Children under 2 must ride rear-facing until they outgrow the maker's height and weight limits.

q: In Pennsylvania, a 6-year-old must ride in:
b: A booster seat with a lap and shoulder belt
d: Any seat, no restraint needed in back
exp: Children 4 to under 8 must use a booster seat with the lap and shoulder belt.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 5, Laws and Related Issues, Child Restraint Law

q: What restraint does Pennsylvania require for a 3-year-old?
d: A seat belt in the back seat
exp: Children under 4 must be in an approved child passenger restraint system.

q: What is the fine for a child restraint violation in Pennsylvania?
exp: Child restraint violations carry a $75 fine.

q: Can Pennsylvania police stop an adult driver only for not wearing a seat belt?
a: No, for adults the belt citation follows a stop for another violation
exp: For adult drivers and front passengers, a belt fine requires a conviction for another violation at the same time.

q: How often must a Pennsylvania passenger car pass a safety inspection?
exp: Safety inspection is required every 12 months at an authorized station.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 5, Laws and Related Issues, Vehicle Safety and Emissions Inspection

q: How early may you have your Pennsylvania safety inspection done before the sticker expires?
d: Only in the month it expires
exp: Vehicles may be inspected up to 90 days before the sticker expires.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 5, Laws and Related Issues, Vehicle Safety and Emissions Inspection

q: What happens if a registered Pennsylvania vehicle goes without insurance for 31 days or more?
c: Nothing if the car is not driven
d: The registration is suspended for 3 months
exp: Lapsed insurance of 31 days or more brings a 3-month registration suspension.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 4, Pennsylvania's Point System, Driving Without Insurance

q: Within how many days must you tell PennDOT about a change of address?
exp: Name and address changes must be reported within 15 days.
src: PA online Driver's Manual, Ch. 5, Laws and Related Issues, Required Notification

q: A driver under 18 has a car with four seat belts. How many people may be in the car, including the driver?
exp: A driver under 18 may not carry more passengers than there are seat belts.

q: Is a Pennsylvania seat belt ticket a moving violation with points?
exp: A seat belt conviction is not a moving violation and assesses no points.

q: How large is the parallel parking space on the Pennsylvania road test?
exp: The space is 24 by 8 feet, marked by upright poles.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Tests, pp. 5 to 6

q: During Pennsylvania road test parallel parking, which mistake causes a fail?
a: Touching one of the upright poles
exp: Touching a pole, crossing the painted line or mounting the curb fails the maneuver.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Tests, pp. 5 to 6

q: Your car can park itself. What does Pennsylvania require on the road test?
a: You must use it for the parallel park
b: The self-parking feature must be turned off
exp: Self-parking cars may be used, but the feature must stay off during the test.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Tests, pp. 5 to 6

q: Who may ride in the car with you during the Pennsylvania road test?
exp: The examiner is your only passenger during the road test.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Tests, pp. 5 to 6

q: If you pass the road test at a PennDOT Driver License Center, when do you get your license?
exp: Passing at a PennDOT center means you receive your license at that time.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Tests, pp. 5 to 6

q: Which item must you bring to the Pennsylvania road test?
a: Proof that the test car is insured
exp: Bring the permit, DL-180C if under 18, the car's registration and insurance, and the accompanying driver's license.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Tests, pp. 5 to 6

q: If you have not passed the road test within three years of your physical exam date, what must you do?
b: Start over with a new DL-180 and retake the knowledge test
exp: After three years from the physical, you must reapply and retake the knowledge test.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Tests, pp. 5 to 6

q: Under 18, how far ahead may you schedule your Pennsylvania road test?
exp: Young drivers may schedule the skills test up to six months in advance.
src: PA Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Ch. 1, Tests, pp. 5 to 6
